title: Copy List with Random Pointer
statement: Each node has a `next` and a `random` pointer (to any node or None). Build a deep copy of the list: all-new nodes whose next/random pointers mirror the original's structure and point only to new nodes. (The checker reports [value, random_index] per node, or an error if any original node is reused.)

hints.1_question: A copy must have its own nodes. The tricky part is random: it points to a node that may not have been copied yet. How can you look up 'the copy of node X'?
hints.2_nudge: Make two passes: first create a copy of every node and remember old -> new in a dictionary; then wire next and random using that map.
hints.3_big_hint: m[old] = Node(old.val) for all nodes. Then m[old].next = m.get(old.next); m[old].random = m.get(old.random). Return m[head].

known_bugs.name: returns the original list (no copy)
known_bugs.followup: If the caller changes the 'copy', does the original change too?

known_bugs.name: copied random pointers still point to original nodes
known_bugs.followup: A copied node's random must point to a copied node. What does it point to here?

known_bugs.name: maps nodes by value (breaks with equal values)
known_bugs.followup: Several nodes can hold the same value. Does a dictionary keyed by value pick the right copy?

followups: How can you do it in O(1) extra space by interleaving copies?
What does the dictionary key identify - value or node?
